stance.label: Short-term bearish · long-term in the bottom zone

headline: Short-term bearish, long-term cheap: 6 closes below the 200-day MA; selling eased but ETFs took in only $9.4M, no new money yet.
summary: Short-term bearish: 64K has held for three days and active selling stopped, but stablecoins are down $16.1B in 30 days and ETFs took in just $9.4M, so the buyers are not new money. Long-term bullish: unrealized profit has sat below the cycle floor for 4 days and the Dawn Index is still in Deep Night, a spot that was higher a year later every time. 62K is still the line: a close below it leaves few short-term holder coins down to 58K.

cycle.lead: Valuation stays in the bottom zone and the trend still points down: Dawn Index heat 7.5, Deep Night; weekly bull-bear score −0.72.
points: Market stage is bull, day 40: the 200-day MA at 72,799 is still rising; 1 of 6 evidence lights is on (exchange supply).
Relative unrealized profit is 34.3%, a fourth day under the 35% floor.
Tidemark bottom signal 36.5, timing 95.3, still short of the 50 threshold; the Jun 30 low at 58,525 is under test until Dec 19.
Day 407 after this cycle's top, down 48.0%; the prior three cycles were all below −75% on the same day.

market.lead: Sell Pressure Index 100 with momentum at 0.10: the bottom combo is still on while price just moves sideways.
points: This combo has occurred 20 times since 2012; 30 days later price was up 11 times with a median of +1.8%, about the same as any day's +3.2%.
The leg from Sep 21 is down 25.1% over 57 days; the leg-end line at 73,732 is 13.6% away.
The close sits at the 19.5th percentile of the past year, with the 10% line at 63,547, 2% below.

deriv.lead: Leverage backed off a little but did not leave: funding fell from 6.5% to 4.7% and 72% of accounts are still long.
points: The funding rebound we wrote about yesterday did not continue: OKX turned negative at −1.2% while Hyperliquid is still at 11%; open interest is down 6.6% in 7 days (Coinalyze).
7-day implied vol 42.2% vs 90-day 40.6%, the inversion down to 1.6 points; 25Δ risk reversal −5.12, downside protection still costs more.
The estimated short-liquidation band at 65.7–67.4K (2.5% above the close) is nearer than the long band at 60.8–62.0K below; estimated from Coinalyze aggregate open interest plus assumed leverage.
Order book: $246M of bids at 64,000 and $184M of asks at 65,000, both on Hyperliquid perps, with price boxed in between.

flows.lead: ETF outflows paused for a day but money is still leaving: stablecoins are down $16.1B in 30 days and realized cap has been below zero for 4 days.
points: This page's finding: ETFs took in $9.4M on Nov 16, ending 7 straight outflow sessions; the 20-day total is −$2.60B, the deepest of this stretch (CoinMarketCap).
Coinbase spot takers net sold 9,732 BTC over 7 days, no smaller than before; across three spot venues the day flipped to 2,510 BTC of net taker buying (Coinalyze).
Korea premium 2.33% → 1.91%, back under 2%.
USDT at 0.9989 to the dollar, its month-to-date average the lowest in 50 months; stablecoin supply $286.4B (DefiLlama).

onchain.lead: Loss-taking is still heavy but no longer growing: short-term holders have sold at a loss for 12 days, and capitulation intensity eased from 5.3 to 4.4.
points: This page's finding: network-wide realized profit ÷ realized loss averaged 0.24 over 7 days, so sellers as a whole are taking losses (CheckOnChain, Nov 17).
Short-term holders realized 11,169 BTC of losses against 1,953 BTC of profit; STH-SOPR 0.970, a touch above yesterday's 0.963.
About 460K BTC moved at a loss over these 7 days, and the 64K bucket gained 280K BTC (Bitview).
Long-term holder loss share is 41.9% vs this cycle's 45.4% peak; an estimated close at 60,500 would exceed it (CheckOnChain).

exit.lead: Under the framework the 20% hedge is bought back today: the MVRV Z 7-day average is 0.48, below 0.5 (CoinMetrics, Nov 16).
points: The 200-day MA rule itself has not changed: 6 straight closes below 72,799, 12.2% under the line.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.437, far from the 0.75 line (111,586); the three top indicators read 12 / 12 / 43, all low.

findings.title: 64K holds a third day: active selling stopped, but the buyers are not new money
findings.lean_why: Selling pressure eased, but ETFs, stablecoins and realized cap are all still draining; a range without new money does not hold for long.
findings.what: Who has been buying at 64K these three days? Money already inside the market changing hands, with no new money coming in: ETFs took in only $9.4M on Nov 16 and stablecoins shrank another 1.35% in 7 days (CoinMarketCap, DefiLlama).
findings.why: Split it into sellers and buyers. Sellers backed off: takers on three spot venues net bought 2,510 BTC on the day and perps 2,635 BTC, after net selling 12K and 69K BTC over the prior 7 days (Coinalyze, Nov 17). Buyers bring no new money: ETFs came back for one day after 7 outflow sessions and the 20-day total is −$2.60B; stablecoins are down $16.1B in 30 days; realized cap is −0.44% over 30 days, a fourth day below zero (CoinMetrics, Nov 16); Coinbase spot takers still net sold 9,732 BTC over 7 days. Where the buying sits is visible: $246M of bids at 64,000 on the order book; by address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 41K BTC in 7 days while the 1K–10K tier shed 33K BTC (Bitview). The cost map is unchanged: the thickest short-term holder layer at 64–66K holds 660K BTC and 62–64K holds 580K BTC, with very little below.
findings.alt: Another reading: sellers are only waiting for the FOMC minutes and the direction of stocks, one day without active selling does not count, and ETFs have had only one inflow day. Address tiers are not entities, and exchange wallet housekeeping moves coins between large and small addresses; Coinalyze spot taker data covers only Binance, Coinbase and Bybit.
findings.history: ETF outflows stopping does not mean the drop is over. Among stretches with 20-day outflows above $1.5B, the deepest was −$5.64B in June 2026 against −$2.60B now; the 30 days after past stretches ended went both ways. Short-term holder capitulation below the 200-day MA has happened 23 times since 2012, with price up 30 days later 10 times.
findings.so: What changed is the sell side: active selling stopped, ETFs stopped bleeding, and the 64–66K layer has takers for now. What did not change is the buy side, with money still leaving through stablecoins and ETFs; without new money, holding here is only a range. Today's framework buy-back looks at valuation and is unrelated to this finding.
findings.next: By Nov 21: 7-day spot taker flow turning positive (now −12,324 BTC) means someone has started chasing price; a close below 62,000 means the buyers of these three days have become sellers too.

findings.title: Coins sold this week were sold at a net loss; the 90-day average has not caught up
findings.lean_why: Sellers as a whole are taking losses; if that persists the 90-day average falls back below 1, the state seen in past bear stretches.
findings.what: The state since September, where sellers as a whole were in profit, has in practice flipped this week: network-wide realized profit ÷ realized loss averaged 0.24 over the last 7 days while the 90-day average still reads 2.3 (CheckOnChain, Nov 17).
findings.why: This rests on onchain.rpl; no signal fired. The 90-day average is slow, so look at the daily ratio first: 0.45 on Nov 11, down to 0.14 on Nov 16, 0.15 on Nov 17. Who is losing: of the last 30 days' realized losses, coins held under 1 month make up 54% and coins held 1–2 years 31% (Bitview); short-term holders realized 11,169 BTC of losses against 1,953 BTC of profit on the day. Net realized P&L lines up: −$6.7B over the last 7 days against −$1.6B the 7 days before (CoinMetrics, Nov 16).
findings.alt: CheckOnChain's numbers are per-UTXO with no entity adjustment, so exchange wallet housekeeping counts as selling at a loss; the daily ratio swings a lot, and one or two days of large profitable moves can pull the 7-day average back above 1. Net realized P&L may be duller in the ETF era because ETF shares change hands off-chain.
findings.history: A 90-day average below 1 is the state of past bear stretches; the latest ran from Feb 7 to Sep 3, 2026, 209 days. Relapses after a recovery have happened: in Dec 2019–Jan 2020 it fell back for 37 days, 7 months after climbing above 1.
findings.so: What changed is how to read the 90-day average of 2.3: October's profits are holding it up, while this week's actual behavior is already loss-taking. What did not change is that it is still above 1, day 74 since Sep 4; neither the market stage nor the framework uses this indicator.
findings.next: By Nov 24: the 7-day average back above 0.5 means loss-taking is fading; below 0.2 means it is still deepening. If the daily ratio stays at 0.24, a trial calculation has the 90-day average falling back to 1 around Jan 1, 2027.

research.summary: Glassnode's Nov 17 weekly matches our readings: losses reached capitulation levels, 62–66K absorbed the selling and takers turned to buying, but stablecoins, miners and ETFs are all still draining; its two lines at 62K and 74.1K are the same as ours.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Capitulation Meets Support
items.points: BTC fell to 62K on Nov 15 and realized losses reached levels not seen since early 2023; 62–66K holds about a fifth of short-term holder coins and grew by 66K BTC on the two heaviest days; the remaining long-liquidation cluster is 59.5–62.2K; bids within 5% of price on Binance and Coinbase outweigh asks 2.3x; ETFs lost $2.6B over ten trading days and MARA and Riot sold about 28K BTC this month; reclaiming 74.1K would look like a bottom forming, a daily close below 62K points to 58.5K and the Realized Price at 53.7K.
items.meaning: The same conclusion as 2026-11-17-1: the selling was absorbed and new demand is still missing. Our wide order book shows $681M of bids against $404M of asks, the same direction; its 74.1K is our short-term holder cost at 74,056.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 47
items.points: BTC fell about 13% on the week and briefly broke 63K; futures open interest at $34.2B is the lowest since August; 25Δ skew at 13.7% is the highest since August; ETF weekly outflow $995M and ETF MVRV 1.06, near break-even; short-term holder NUPL −7.4%; it concludes leverage was flushed and the market is less crowded.
items.meaning: Our weighted funding was 4.65% on Nov 17 with 72% of accounts long, more crowded than when it was written; our estimated ETF holder cost is 17.8% above the close, already underwater on our numbers.

items.title: Bitcoin Back Where the Rally Began
items.points: BTC fell for a sixth straight week, back to the July base at 61,300–67,000; about 1.40M BTC were acquired at 60–65K and only about 305K BTC at 55–60K; base case this week is 61,800–69,400 with risk skewed to a retest of 62,029; a recovery needs three straight ETF inflow sessions, STH-SOPR back toward 1 and a reclaim of 72,700.
items.meaning: Its supply gap matches ours: very little below 62K. None of its three recovery conditions is met today, with one ETF inflow day and STH-SOPR at 0.970.
